topics.answer: The work is called Management Fee Calculation & Offsets; the supplied workbook is named F05 MC-05 workbook.xlsx.
The documented work produces an approved management-fee calculation, funded or collected and posted fees, and a reconciled records package.
The initiating event and normal cadence are not specified; asked what starts the work, the participant had nothing to add to the workbook. Deadlines are explicitly unconfirmed in its notes.

The workbook requires posted and funded amounts to equal the approved calculation, and the GL, calculation, notices, workbooks and funding to agree. The final package is filed with the supporting rule versions, inputs, review, approval, funding, posting and reconciliation.
The accountable owner and named reviewer and approver are unconfirmed; the workbook identifies functional participants but does not assign overall accountability.

According to the workbook, the GPFS preparer identifies the billing period and advance, arrears or stub treatment and checks for rule changes; the reviewer and client confirm. Rules in effect and supporting terms are recorded, and unclear or overlapping rules are resolved before calculation.
The preparer gathers fee-base inputs, investor lists, offset amounts, waiver elections, related contribution rollforwards, caps and side-letter exceptions. The preparer reconciles offsets to sources and prior offsets, waivers and carryforwards to the previous standalone calculation and GL, resolving or documenting differences; missing adviser or client terms stop the affected calculation.
The preparer applies fund- and investor-specific bases and rates for each effective time segment, approved annualization and proration, and applicable investor rules; gross investor fees are reconciled to fund totals. The preparer then applies offsets, waivers, caps and approved carryforwards and calculates net investor fees using the validated negative-fee rule.
The senior reviewer reviews the calculation and reconciles copies; comments are resolved and client approval obtained before the final approved version is identified. Fund accounting and capital-call teams fund or collect and post using permitted methods, although their exact downstream roles are not specified.
The GPFS preparer and reviewer reconcile the final standalone calculation to the GL and later notice and workbook outputs, and file the package in the digital binder Q folder.

The workbook assigns the preparer effective-rule, source/prior-balance and investor-to-fund ties, reviewed by a reviewer. It assigns the reviewer the offset-to-source and LPA reconciliation, approved-version control, and approval-to-posting tie.
The senior reviewer reviews rules, bases, groups, formulas, offsets, waivers, rollforwards and GL reconciliations. A two-person review is required for a step-down or fee-base change; comments are resolved and client approval obtained, with duplicates agreeing with or linking to the approved version.
Named reviewers and approvers, approval evidence and handling of rejected or delayed approvals need confirmation.

The workbook describes different billing treatments for advance, arrears and stub periods, and fund- and investor-specific bases, rates, side-letter and other rules. Funding can use an LPA-permitted capital call, fund cash or netting; the method for each fund is unconfirmed.

F05 MC-05 workbook.xlsx contains steps, checks and a hidden notes sheet. The participant says the file describes current practice but adds nothing; its notes retain explicit open items. All three indexed text sections were supplied and reviewed; no unread visuals are reported.
The documented working artifacts include a rules record and supporting terms, reconciled input package, investor gross-fee schedule, offset and net-fee schedule, approved standalone calculation and final records package.
The exact digital binder path and retention period are unconfirmed, although the workbook names a Q folder.

The workbook describes GPFS preparation of fund- and investor-specific management fees, client approval and downstream funding and posting. The participant says it describes today's work; whether it is a general GPFS route or a particular client route is not established.

The documented rule is to check effective dates, retain supporting terms, resolve overlaps before calculation and not carry forward a prior-period rule without checking its date. Offset allocation uses the LPA rule, applicable fund and portfolio-company list, percentage and timing; approved delays, waiver caps and carryforwards are applied.
The workbook leaves Standard Days, annualization, stub and proration rules, negative fees, carryforwards, rounding, waiver/contribution interaction and offset delays unconfirmed. It says not to use generic formulas until Standard Days and annualization are confirmed.
The exact debit and credit accounts and accounting entries must be confirmed; funding methods for each fund are also unconfirmed.
The documented calculation requires client approval before fund accounting and capital-call teams fund or collect and post the approved fee; the split between downstream roles is not specified.

The workbook requires reconciliation to the GL, previous standalone calculation and later notices and workbook outputs, with filing in a digital binder Q folder.
Source-system reports and the exact digital binder path are unconfirmed; the calculation tool and its logic ownership are not identified.

steps.title: Confirm period and rules
steps.actor: GPFS preparer; reviewer and client confirm
steps.description: The workbook directs the preparer to identify the billing period and advance, arrears or stub treatment. Check closes, step-downs, investment-period end, impairments, waivers, holidays, start-date overrides and amendments. Record the rules in effect and retain supporting terms; do not change the rules during the calculation or carry a prior-period rule forward without checking its effective date. Resolve unclear or overlapping rules before calculating.

steps.title: Gather and reconcile inputs
steps.description: The workbook calls for obtaining commitments, contributions, invested capital or NAV and the investor list under the approved fee-base definition. Reconcile monitoring fees and other offsets to sources; obtain waiver elections, lifetime-to-date related contribution rollforwards, caps and side-letter exceptions. Reconcile prior offsets, waivers and carryforwards to the previous standalone calculation and GL, and resolve or document every difference. Missing adviser or client terms stop the affected calculation.

steps.title: Hold affected calculation
steps.description: The workbook says to stop the affected calculation if adviser or client terms are missing. The release condition and subsequent handoff are UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Calculate gross investor fees
steps.description: The workbook directs the preparer to apply each fund- and investor-specific fee base and rate to each effective time segment, with approved annualization, proration and stub rules. Apply side-letter, class, holiday, exclusion, start-date and step-down rules. Reconcile investor gross fees to fund totals and trace every calculation to an effective rule and source fee base. Do not use generic formulas until Standard Days and annualization are confirmed.

steps.title: Apply offsets and waivers
steps.description: The workbook directs allocation of each offset type using its LPA rule, applicable fund and portfolio-company list, percentage and timing. Apply monitoring-fee offsets in the correct period, including approved delays; apply waiver elections and caps on related contributions or excess costs. Apply approved carryforwards and move any remaining approved amount to the next period. Calculate net fees using the validated rule for nonnegative or negative fees. Reconcile offsets and waivers to sources and check for overlapping rules for the same scope and dates.

steps.title: Review fee calculation
steps.description: The workbook calls for review of rules, fee bases, groups, formulas, offsets, waivers, rollforwards and GL reconciliations, and reconciliation of the standalone calculation to capital-call or quarterly copies. It requires two-person review for periods with a step-down or fee-base change and resolution of comments. The Checks sheet assigns the reviewer the offset-to-source and LPA reconciliation.

steps.title: Obtain client approval
steps.description: The workbook requires client approval, identification of the final approved version and confirmation that every duplicate agrees with it or links to it. The Checks sheet assigns version control to the reviewer. How approval is requested and rejection or delay handled is UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Fund or collect and post
steps.actor: Fund accounting and capital-call teams; exact downstream roles UNKNOWN
steps.description: The workbook directs use of the LPA-allowed method: capital call, fund cash or netting. Use the approved accounting pattern: expense and cash, expense and payable, or an amount Due to Manager. Confirm exact debit and credit accounts before posting. Reconcile funded or collected amounts and entries to the approved calculation; posted and funded amounts must equal it.

steps.title: Reconcile and file package
steps.description: The workbook calls for reconciling the final standalone calculation to the GL and later notices and workbook outputs, and filing the package in the digital binder Q folder. Retain rule versions, inputs, review, approval, funding, posting and reconciliation. The GL, calculation, notices, workbooks and funding must agree. The Checks sheet assigns the approval-to-posting tie to the reviewer at completion; the exact binder path and retention period are unconfirmed.
